patch_description: The original code was deeply broken: it mutated/merged columns (col_merge paths changed shapes), returned an empty column_orderings list (invalid per-row orderings), fabricated an "original_index" column, reordered via fragile itertuples/attribute lookups, used threading with non-deterministic row assignment (futures assigned by as_completed index), and its final sort reordered rows without consistent per-row column orders. The fix replaces the entire editable block with a simple, correct, deterministic implementation: serialize each cell to its scoring string once, build up to three cheap candidate per-row column orderings (frequency-ranked global order, length-weighted count*(count-1) order, original order), score each candidate exactly via the sorted-string adjacent-LCP sum (computed with C-speed prefix binary search), pick the best, then output the permuted dataframe (object dtype for mixed types) together with valid per-row column orderings. No data is added, dropped, fabricated or altered; col_merge columns are kept adjacent (merged values are pre-joined by the evaluator semantics, so we only keep their relative order); row/column stops and early_stop are honored as bounds on work.
